summary: Shivram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Shankashastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (~1955–1960). He held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1960–1987) and Deccan College (~1987–1996).

Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University, under Jikido Takasaki. He has held positions at Hanazono University as lecturer (1990), associate professor (1992), and professor (2002).

Shlomo Pines was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin (1926–1934). He taught at the University of Paris and the Institut d'Histoire des Sciences et des Techniques before serving at Hebrew University (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky worked in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1920–1922) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1922–1924), and held a post at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).

Shobha Rani Dash is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She was a researcher at Ryukoku University (2010), a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and professor at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).
Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Shofuku-ji and under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982). He became abbot at Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamakami is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (until 1964). He served as associate professor (attested 1979–1988) and professor (attested 1995) at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Shogo Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology and studied at Toyo University. He served as professor at Toyo University (attested 2003–2015) and held later posts at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Taisho University (attested 2026).

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama. He served at Pioneer Valley Zendo, Kyoto Soto Zen Center, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa worked in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1950–1955) and held a post at The Open University of Japan.

Shoji Mori was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi. He held positions at Toyo University as associate professor (attested 1980–1981) and professor (attested 1995–1998), and at Okurayama Institute.

Shoji Muramoto works in philosophy and religious studies and studied at Kyoto University and the University of Zurich. Muramoto held posts at Hanazono University and Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2002–2009).
Shoju Inaba was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Otani University (attested 1962) and part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956). He held posts at Ueno Gakuen University and Otani University (~1968–2000).

Shokin Furuta worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki and at Tokyo University and Tokyo University of Education. He held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1953–1963) and Nihon University (~1963–1982), and directed Matsugaoka Bunko (1966).
Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post as professor at Toyo University (attested 1987, 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Taisho University (1948–1955). He served as lecturer (1960), associate professor (1962), and Dean of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002) at Taisho University.

Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata holds posts as lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and later served as professor emeritus there (attested 1987–1995).
